copy.en:
How do scientists study black holes and gravity?

They use them as natural laboratories! For example, they detected ripples called gravitational waves when two black holes merged far out in space.
copy.tl:
Paano pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentista ang mga black hole at grabidad?

Ginagamit nila ito bilang likas na laboratoryo! Halimbawa, nadama nila ang mga alon ng grabidad noong dalawang black hole ang nagsanib sa malayong kalawakan.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtuon sa mga siyentista sa mga black hole ug grabidad?

Gigamit nila kini isip natural nga laboratoryo! Pananglitan, ilang nasabtan ang gravitational waves dihang duha ka black hole nagtipon sa layong kawanangan.

How did scientists take the first-ever photo of a black hole?

In 2019, telescopes around the world worked together! They captured a picture showing a dark center ringed by glowing gas.
copy.tl:
Paano nakuha ng mga siyentista ang kauna-unahang larawan ng black hole?

Noong 2019, nagtulungan ang mga teleskopyo sa buong mundo! Nakuha nila ang larawan ng madilim na gitna na napapalibutan ng nagliliwanag na gas.
copy.bis:
Giunsa nakuha sa mga siyentista ang unang litrato sa black hole?

Niadtong 2019, nagtinabangay ang mga teleskopyo sa tibuok kalibutan! Nakuha nila ang litrato sa ngitngit nga tunga nga gilibutan og nagsiga nga gas.

copy.en: A black hole grows bigger by pulling in gas, dust, and even stars! It also gets huge when two black holes merge into one.
copy.tl: Lumalaki ang black hole sa pamamagitan ng paghila ng gas, alikabok, at kahit mga bituin! Lumalaki rin ito kapag dalawang black hole ang nagsanib.
copy.bis: Modako ang black hole pinaagi sa pagbira og gas, abog, ug bisan mga bituon! Modako usab kini kon duha ka black hole magtipon ug mahimong usa.

copy.tl: Ayon sa mga ideya ni Einstein, mas mabagal ang oras malapit sa malakas na grabidad ng black hole! Kaya magkaiba ang takbo ng orasan sa iba't ibang lugar.
copy.bis: Sumala sa mga ideya ni Einstein, mohinay ang oras duol sa kusog nga grabidad sa black hole! Mao nga lahi ang dagan sa relo sa lainlaing dapit.

copy.bis: Ang siyentista nga si Elizabeth Blackburn nakadiskubre sa enzyme nga telomerase ug kon unsaon kini pagmentinar sa mga tumoy sa chromosome, busa nakadaog siya ug Nobel Prize sa Medicine niadtong 2009.

Bakit may mga kwarto na gumagamit ng napakakapal at maitim na kurtina?

Ang blackout curtains ay mga opaque na materyales na humaharang sa liwanag nang tuluyan, kaya nananatiling madilim ang kwarto kahit maliwanag ang araw sa labas.
copy.bis:
Ngano ang uban nga kwarto naggamit ug baga kaayo ug itom nga kurtina?

Ang blackout curtains kay mga opaque nga materyales nga nagbabag sa kahayag sa hingpit, mao nga magpabilin nga ngitngit ang kwarto bisan pa hayag ang adlaw sa gawas.

copy.bis: Ang atmosphere sa Earth usa ka habol sa mga gas, kasagaran nitrogen ug oxygen, nga nagpaposible sa kinabuhi kay naghatag kinig hangin nga atong giginhawa ug proteksyon batok sa makadaot nga silaw sa adlaw.

copy.en: Vapors from liquid bleach irritate the nose, throat, and lungs, so use it in a well-ventilated area.

copy.bis: Ang alisngaw gikan sa liquid bleach makapalagot sa ilong, tutunlan, ug baga, busa gamita kini sa lugar nga maayo ang bentilasyon.

copy.bis: Ang matag mata adunay blind spot diin walay rods o cones! Kini ang lugar diin mogawas ang optic nerve, mao nga walay suga nga nasensasan didto.

assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address growth, response, or reproduction, the characteristics of living things in the competency.

copy.en: Your brain needs enough sleep to control your body well. Without it, you focus less, decide slower, and make more mistakes.
copy.tl: Kailangan ng utak ng sapat na tulog para mahusay na makontrol ang katawan. Kung puyat, nahihirapan itong mag-focus at magdesisyon, kaya mas madalas kang magkamali.
copy.bis: Nanginahanglan ang utok og igong tulog aron maayong makontrol ang lawas. Kon kulang tulog, maglisod kini mag-focus ug magdesisyon, mao nga mas sayon ka masayop.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the left side of your brain controls the right side of your body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes brain lateralization (nervous system), not any of the human body systems listed in G4-L-1 (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). It does not support the competency.

copy.en:
Which brain side controls your right hand?

Surprisingly, the left side of your brain controls the right side of your body, and the right side controls the left!
copy.tl:
Aling bahagi ng utak ang kumokontrol sa kanang kamay mo?

Nakakatuwang malaman na ang kaliwang bahagi ng utak ang kumokontrol sa kanang bahagi ng katawan, at ang kanan naman ay sa kaliwa!
copy.bis:
Unsang bahin sa utok ang nagkontrol sa imong tuo nga kamot?

Makalingaw nga ang wala nga bahin sa utok ang nagkontrol sa tuo nga bahin sa lawas, ug ang tuo nagkontrol sa wala!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If the part of the brain that controls a body part is damaged, that body part may stop working
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: Brain damage is unrelated to living things interacting through competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If the part of the brain that controls a body part is damaged, that body part may stop working, like legs that cannot move
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: Brain damage is unrelated to how living things depend on one another to meet their basic needs.

copy.en:
What happens if the brain gets damaged?

If the part of the brain that controls a body part is damaged, that body part may stop working, like legs that cannot move!
copy.tl:
Ano ang mangyayari kapag nasira ang utak?

Kapag nasira ang bahagi ng utak na kumokontrol sa isang bahagi ng katawan, maaaring huminto sa paggana ang bahaging iyon, tulad ng mga binti na hindi makagalaw!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mahitabo kung madaot ang utok?

Kung madaot ang parte sa utok nga nagkontrol sa usa ka parte sa lawas, mahimong mohunong sa paglihok kana nga parte, sama sa mga batiis nga dili makalihok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each eye has a tiny 'blind spot' that sees nothing at all
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the eye and brain's visual perception, not any of the specified body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). It does not support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each eye has a tiny 'blind spot' that sees nothing at all
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It is about visual perception and the brain's filling-in mechanism, unrelated to this competency.

copy.en:
Why don't you notice your eye's blind spot?

Each eye has a tiny 'blind spot' that sees nothing at all, but your brain fills in the gap so you never notice a hole in what you're looking at.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi mo napapansin ang blind spot ng mata mo?

May maliit na 'blind spot' ang bawat mata na walang nakikita, pero pinupunan ito ng utak kaya hindi mo napapansin ang butas sa tinitingnan mo.
copy.bis:
Nganong dili nimo mabantayan ang blind spot sa imong mata?

Ang matag mata adunay gamay nga 'blind spot' nga walay makita, apan sapnayan kini sa utok mao nga dili nimo mamatikdan ang lungag sa imong gitan-aw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The brain itself feels no pain because it has no pain sensors
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the brain's lack of pain receptors, which is a nervous system topic. G4-L-1 requires describing the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. The brain is not part of any of these systems, so the card does not support the competency.

copy.en:
Can your brain feel pain?

No! The brain itself feels no pain because it has no pain sensors — it senses pain everywhere else in the body, but never in itself.
copy.tl:
Nakakaramdam ba ng sakit ang utak?

Hindi! Ang utak mismo ay walang nararamdamang sakit dahil wala itong pain sensor — ito ang nakakaramdam ng sakit sa ibang bahagi ng katawan, pero hindi sa sarili nito.
copy.bis:
Makabati ba og kasakit ang utok?

Dili! Ang utok mismo walay mabati nga kasakit kay wala kini pain sensor — kini ang mobati sa kasakit sa ubang bahin sa lawas, apan dili sa kaugalingon niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The adult human brain weighs only about 2.5 to 3 pounds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about brain weight, which is unrelated to examining weather charts, interpreting local weather, or practicing safety precautions during poor weather. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: The adult human brain weighs only about 2.5 to 3 pounds, yet it controls the whole body!
copy.tl: Ang brain ng adult na tao ay tumitimbang lamang ng mga 2.5 hanggang 3 pounds, pero kontrolado nito ang buong katawan!
copy.bis: Ang brain sa adult nga tao motimbang lamang ug mga 2.5 hangtod 3 pounds, apan kontrolado niya ang tibuok lawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A switch in one branch of a parallel circuit controls only the components on that branch, not the whole circuit.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of covalent bonds using a molecule of water and a molecule of carbon dioxide
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about parallel circuit switch behavior, which is electricity/circuits content. G9-M-7 is about covalent bond formation in water and carbon dioxide, a chemistry topic with no connection to circuits.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A switch in one branch of a parallel circuit controls only the components on that branch, not the whole circuit.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical name of some common covalent compounds, including water (H2O), carbon dioxide (CO2), and ammonia (NH3)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses parallel circuit branch switching, not chemical formulas or names of covalent compounds. G9-M-8 is entirely unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en: A switch in one branch of a parallel circuit controls only the components on that branch, not the whole circuit.
copy.tl: Ang switch sa isang sanga ng parallel circuit ay kumokontrol lamang sa mga bahagi sa sanga na iyon, hindi sa buong circuit.
copy.bis: Ang switch sa usa ka sanga sa parallel circuit nagkontrol lamang sa mga parte sa maong sanga, dili sa tibuok circuit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The bronchi and bronchioles are branching air tubes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify practical applications of electromagnetic radiation, such as radio waves used in telecommunications, and x-rays and gamma rays in medicine
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the anatomy and function of bronchi and bronchioles in the respiratory system. G9-F-12 requires identifying practical applications of electromagnetic radiation (e.g., radio waves, x-rays, gamma rays). There is no connection to electromagnetic radiation or its applications; the content is entirely unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: The bronchi and bronchioles are branching air tubes that carry air from the trachea into every part of the lungs, like roads spreading through a city.
copy.tl: Ang bronchi at bronchioles ay mga sumasangang tubo ng hangin na nagdadala ng hangin mula sa trachea papunta sa bawat bahagi ng baga, parang mga kalsadang kumakalat sa isang lungsod.
copy.bis: Ang bronchi ug bronchioles mao ang nagsanga-sanga nga mga tubo sa hangin nga nagdala sa hangin gikan sa trachea ngadto sa matag parte sa baga, sama sa mga dalan nga nagkatag sa usa ka siyudad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Arteries branch into smaller vessels called arterioles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the branching of arteries into arterioles and capillaries, which is circulatory system anatomy. It has no relation to gravity or the motion of objects under gravity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Arteries branch into smaller vessels called arterioles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about blood vessel structure, not about gravity as a non-contact force. No instructional support for identifying gravity's effects.

copy.en: Arteries branch into smaller vessels called arterioles, which then enter tissues and branch into the smallest blood vessels, the capillaries.
copy.tl: Ang arteries ay sumasanga sa mas maliliit na vessels na tinatawag na arterioles, na pumapasok sa tissues at sumasanga sa pinakamaliit na blood vessels, ang capillaries.
copy.bis: Ang arteries nagsanga ngadto sa gagmay nga mga vessels nga gitawag ug arterioles, nga mosulod sa tissues ug nagsanga ngadto sa pinakagamay nga blood vessels, ang capillaries.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brass and steel are metals that are good heat conductors
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes brass and steel as heat-conducting metals used in kitchenware and tools. It does not address subatomic particles (protons, neutrons, electrons), their symbols, mass, charge, or location within an atom, which is the focus of G8-M-3.

copy.en: Brass and steel are metals that are good heat conductors, often used in kitchenware and tools.
copy.tl: Ang brass at steel ay mga metal na mahuhusay na heat conductors, kadalasang ginagamit sa mga kagamitan sa kusina at tools.
copy.bis: Ang brass ug steel mga metal nga maayo nga heat conductors, kasagarang gigamit sa mga gamit sa kusina ug tools.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mountain ranges in Brazil and Ghana agree over the Atlantic Ocean, showing these continents were once connected.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the relationship among force, acceleration, and mass
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes geological evidence for continental drift (matching mountain ranges across the Atlantic), which is unrelated to the competency about investigating the relationship among force, acceleration, and mass. This is a physics/mechanics competency, and the card provides no instructional support for it.

copy.en: Mountain ranges in Brazil and Ghana agree over the Atlantic Ocean, showing these continents were once connected.
copy.tl: Ang mga bulubundukin sa Brazil at Ghana ay magkatugma sa kabila ng Atlantic Ocean, na nagpapakitang dating magkadikit ang mga kontinenteng ito.
copy.bis: Ang mga kabukiran sa Brazil ug Ghana nagkatakdo tabok sa Atlantic Ocean, nga nagpakita nga kaniadto nagkahiusa kining mga kontinente.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Circuit breakers and fuses in a house are connected in parallel to protect different parts of the home wiring separately.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the properties of ionic, covalent, and metallic substances, such as melting point, hardness, electrical and thermal conductivity
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes electrical safety devices (circuit breakers and fuses) and their parallel connection in home wiring. It does not address the properties of ionic, covalent, or metallic substances such as melting point, hardness, or electrical/thermal conductivity. The content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Circuit breakers and fuses in a house are connected in parallel to protect different parts of the home wiring separately.
copy.tl: Ang mga circuit breaker at fuse sa bahay ay nakakabit nang naka-parallel para protektahan ang iba't ibang bahagi ng wiring ng bahay nang hiwalay.
copy.bis: Ang mga circuit breaker ug fuse sa balay konektado nga naka-parallel aron protektahan ang lain-laing parte sa wiring sa balay nga bulag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The air that comes out of your mouth when you breathe out is also a gas
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes breath as a gas, which is a matter/state-of-matter concept, not gravity as a non-contact force. It provides no information about gravity or its predictable effects on objects, so it does not support the competency.

copy.en: The air that comes out of your mouth when you breathe out is also a gas, and you can feel it when you blow on your hand.
copy.tl: Ang hangin na lumalabas sa iyong bibig kapag humihinga ka palabas ay gas din, at nararamdaman mo ito kapag humihip ka sa iyong kamay.
copy.bis: Ang hangin nga mogawas sa imong baba kung moginhawa ka pagawas kay gas usab, ug mabati nimo kini kung mohuyop ka sa imong kamot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cover their nose with a wet piece of cloth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives safety advice for people with breathing problems during a volcanic ash shower. It contains no mention of units such as milligrams, grams, kilograms, or degrees centigrade, nor any measurement activity. The competency is about identifying and using units in simple science activities, which is entirely unrelated to the card content.

copy.en: Give priority for evacuation outside the area of ash shower to persons with breathing problems, and advise them to cover their nose with a wet piece of cloth.
copy.tl: Unahing ilikas palabas ng lugar na may ash shower ang mga taong may problema sa paghinga, at payuhan silang takpan ang kanilang ilong ng basang tela.
copy.bis: Unahon pagbakwit gawas sa lugar nga adunay ash shower ang mga tawo nga adunay problema sa pagginhawa, ug tambagi sila nga tabonan ang ilang ilong og basa nga panapton.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Clay is shaped into blocks and baked to make bricks for walls
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes clay being shaped and baked into bricks and tiles. It has no content about static electricity, combs, plastic/glass rods, or balloons. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card's subject.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Clay is shaped into blocks and baked to make bricks for walls
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses clay as a material for bricks and tiles, not electrical circuits, conductors, or insulators. There is no instructional support for designing or constructing a circuit or testing conductivity.

copy.en: Clay is shaped into blocks and baked to make bricks for walls, and it is also pressed flat to make tiles for floors.
copy.tl: Ang clay ay hinuhubog na parang blocks at inihurno para maging bricks sa pader, at pinipisil din ito nang patag para maging tiles sa sahig.
copy.bis: Ang clay gihulma nga sama sa blocks ug giluto aron mahimong bricks sa bungbong, ug gipislit usab kini nga patag aron mahimong tiles sa salog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ionic compounds are hard but brittle
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires observing and recording weather changes and describing local weather patterns. The card discusses the brittleness of ionic compounds, a chemistry concept unrelated to weather or earth/space science.

copy.en: Ionic compounds are hard but brittle, so a strong hit can shift their crystal lattice and make them crack or break.
copy.tl: Ang mga ionic compound ay matigas ngunit brittle, kaya ang malakas na pagtama ay maaaring maglipat ng kanilang crystal lattice at maging dahilan ng pagkabasag nito.
copy.bis: Ang mga ionic compound gahi apan brittle, mao nga ang kusog nga pagbunal makabalhin sa ilang crystal lattice ug makapabuak kanila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brittle materials like crayons, pencils, and little twigs break easily when you try to bend or hammer them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the physical property of brittleness in everyday objects. It has no connection to weather disturbances in or near the Philippines, which is the subject of G5-E-8.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brittle materials like crayons, pencils, and little twigs break easily when you try to bend or hammer them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about material properties, not about typical weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone. It provides no instructional support for G5-E-10.

copy.en: Brittle materials like crayons, pencils, and little twigs break easily when you try to bend or hammer them.
copy.tl: Ang mga brittle na materyales tulad ng crayons, lapis, at maliliit na sanga ay madaling maputol kapag sinubukan mong baluktutin o martilyuhin.
copy.bis: Ang mga brittle nga materyales sama sa crayons, lapis, ug gagmay nga mga sanga dali ra maputol kon imong sulayan nga balikon o martilyohon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Angiosperms typically have flat and broad leaves that catch plenty of sunlight for making food.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a physical model or use drawings to demonstrate how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit around the Sun affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas of Earth over a year
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes angiosperm leaf shape and its role in photosynthesis. G7-E-10 requires demonstrating how Earth's tilt relative to its orbit affects sunlight intensity across different areas over a year. There is no connection to Earth's tilt, seasons, or solar intensity distribution.

copy.en: Angiosperms typically have flat and broad leaves that catch plenty of sunlight for making food.
copy.tl: Ang mga angiosperm ay karaniwang may patag at malalapad na dahon na sumasalo ng maraming sikat ng araw para makagawa ng pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang mga angiosperm sagad adunay lapad ug dako nga mga dahon nga makasalo ug daghang kahayag sa adlaw aron makahimo ug pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brown rice keeps its bran skin packed with fiber and nutrients
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires observing outer plant parts (leaves, roots, stems) and their role in water/nutrient uptake from soil. The card discusses the nutritional difference between brown and white rice, focusing on the bran layer of a grain. It does not address leaves, roots, stems, or soil nutrient uptake, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en:
Why is brown rice more nutritious?

Brown rice keeps its bran skin packed with fiber and nutrients, but white rice has that skin removed — leaving fewer nutrients behind.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas masustansya ang brown rice?

Nananatili sa brown rice ang balat nitong puno ng hibla at sustansya, pero tinatanggal ito sa white rice — kaya mas kaunti ang sustansyang naiiwan.
copy.bis:
Ngano mas nutrisyoso ang brown rice?

Nagpabilin sa brown rice ang panit niini nga puno sa hibla ug sustansya, apan gikuhaan kini sa white rice — busa mas gamay ang sustansya nga nahibilin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brushing your teeth twice a day washes away bacteria and food bits that can cause tooth decay.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about oral hygiene and preventing tooth decay, not about describing how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work. It does not support the competency's content.

copy.en: Brushing your teeth twice a day washes away bacteria and food bits that can cause tooth decay.
copy.tl: Ang pagsisipilyo ng ngipin nang dalawang beses sa isang araw ay nag-aalis ng bacteria at tira ng pagkain na sanhi ng pagkabulok ng ngipin.
copy.bis: Ang pagsipilyo sa ngipon kaduha sa usa ka adlaw makuha ang bacteria ug salin sa pagkaon nga hinungdan sa pagkabungaw sa ngipon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brushing your tongue, not just your teeth, helps remove bacteria and keeps your breath from smelling bad.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about oral hygiene (cleaning the tongue to remove bacteria and prevent bad breath). It does not identify any parts of the digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) nor describe how they work, and it does not use pictures or labeled diagrams as required by the competency.

copy.en: Brushing your tongue, not just your teeth, helps remove bacteria and keeps your breath from smelling bad.
copy.tl: Ang paglilinis ng dila kapag nagsisipilyo ay nakakatulong tanggalin ang bakterya at pigilan ang mabahong hininga.
copy.bis: Ang paglimpyo sa dila kung mosipilyo makatabang sa pagkuha sa bakterya ug paglikay sa baho nga gininhawa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brush your teeth twice a day to remove plaque and bacteria
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about oral hygiene (brushing teeth to remove plaque and bacteria). It does not describe how any of the listed human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. Teeth are not part of the skeletal system in the sense of the competency, and the card provides no information about system function.

copy.en: Brush your teeth twice a day to remove plaque and bacteria and keep your smile healthy.
copy.tl: Magsipilyo ng ngipin nang dalawang beses sa isang araw para maalis ang plaka at bakterya.
copy.bis: Magkepilyo sa ngipon kaduha sa usa ka adlaw aron makuha ang plaka ug bakterya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brush your teeth for at least two minutes, twice a day
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about toothbrushing technique and oral hygiene, not about identifying parts of the digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, etc.) or describing how they work. No digestive system content is taught.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brush your teeth for at least two minutes, twice a day
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe how any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) works. It only gives dental care advice, which is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Brush your teeth for at least two minutes, twice a day — use a soft brush and gentle circular motions on every tooth and your gums.
copy.tl: Magsipilyo nang hindi bababa sa dalawang minuto, dalawang beses sa isang araw — gumamit ng malambot na sipilyo at pabilog na kilos sa bawat ngipin at gilagid.
copy.bis: Mag-brush ug dili moubos sa duha ka minuto, makaduha sa usa ka adlaw — gamita ang humok nga brush ug pabilog nga lihok sa matag ngipon ug gilagid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Budding may form a new adult that stays attached to the original body or breaks away to live separately.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes budding, a form of asexual reproduction in organisms. G10-M-8 concerns factors affecting rates of chemical reactions applied to food preservation, materials production, fire control, pollution, and corrosion. There is no chemical reaction or rate-of-reaction content; the topic is entirely biological and unrelated.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In budding, a small copy of the parent grows out from its body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes budding, a form of asexual reproduction in living organisms. G7-M-3 concerns the particle model of matter (particles in motion, spacing, attraction, temperature effects). There is no instructional support for the competency; the topic is entirely unrelated.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In budding, a small copy of the parent grows out from its body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about budding offspring, not about changes of state (solid-liquid-vapor) or particle arrangement/energy changes. The content does not support G7-M-5 in any way.

copy.en: In budding, a small copy of the parent grows out from its body, then breaks off to live on its own as a new individual.
copy.tl: Sa budding, isang maliit na kopya ng magulang ang tumutubo mula sa katawan nito, pagkatapos ay humihiwalay upang mabuhay nang mag-isa bilang bagong indibidwal.
copy.bis: Sa budding, usa ka gamay nga kopya sa ginikanan ang motubo gikan sa lawas niini, dayon mobulag aron mabuhi nga mag-inusara isip bag-ong indibidwal.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Buffer systems regulate the pH of biological fluids like blood by neutralizing extra acid or base to keep the pH steady.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how buffer systems maintain pH in biological fluids. G10-M-8 requires explaining factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied to food preservation, materials production, fire control, pollution, and corrosion. The card does not address reaction rates or any of those applications; it is about acid-base equilibrium, not reaction kinetics.

copy.en: Buffer systems regulate the pH of biological fluids like blood by neutralizing extra acid or base to keep the pH steady.
copy.tl: Ang buffer systems ay nagre-regulate ng pH ng biological fluids tulad ng dugo sa pamamagitan ng pag-neutralize ng sobrang acid o base para manatiling steady ang pH.
copy.bis: Ang buffer systems nag-regulate sa pH sa biological fluids sama sa dugo pinaagi sa pag-neutralize sa sobra nga acid o base aron magpabiling steady ang pH.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Anabolic reactions build larger molecules, like making muscle, while catabolic reactions break down molecules, like digesting rice into sugar.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about physical changes to solid materials (shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, cut) making them useful. The card describes biological anabolic and catabolic chemical reactions in the body, which are unrelated to changes in solid materials. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Does my body build things up and break things down at the same time?\n\nYes! Anabolic reactions build larger molecules, like making muscle, while catabolic reactions break down molecules, like digesting rice into sugar.
